title: Clifford P. Hansen Federal Courthouse Conveyance Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the Senate on September 9, 2014. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Clifford P. Hansen Federal Courthouse Conveyance Act - Directs the Administrator of General Services (GSA) to offer to convey to Teton County, Wyoming, the parcel of land located at 145 East Simpson Street, Jackson, Wyoming, and the building on such land known as the Clifford P. Hansen Federal Courthouse.

Directs the Administrator to require the County to pay: (1) nominal consideration for the parcel, and (2) fair market value for the building.

Allows the Administrator, in lieu of the County's payment for the building, to accept any credits or waivers against lease payments, amounts expended by the County under facility maintenance agreements, or other charges for the continued occupancy or use by the federal government.

Requires the deed for conveyance to include a covenant providing that the parcel and building will be for public use.

Requires proceeds from the conveyance to be paid into the Federal Buildings Fund.

summary.headline: This law directs the federal government to offer Teton County, Wyoming, the Clifford P. Hansen Federal Courthouse building and its land in Jackson.
summary.what_it_does: The General Services Administration must offer to transfer the land at 145 East Simpson Street and the courthouse building to Teton County. The county would pay nominal consideration for the land and fair market value for the building, though the government may accept credits or waivers for lease, maintenance, or occupancy charges instead of cash for the building. The deed must require that the property stay open for public use, and sale proceeds go into the Federal Buildings Fund.

who_it_affects.how: The county would be offered ownership of the courthouse land and building and would have to pay nominal money for the land and fair market value for the building, or offset that cost with credits or waivers.

who_it_affects.group: The General Services Administration and the federal government
who_it_affects.how: The agency must make the offer, set the payment terms, and send the conveyance proceeds to the Federal Buildings Fund.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the public who use the courthouse property
who_it_affects.how: The deed must include a promise that the land and building will remain for public use.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on November 26, 2014, but the summary does not give a specific date for completing the transfer.
